subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Why Insurance Feels Worth It
description: One-minute skill: Why Insurance Feels Worth It.

hook.text: You pay $1,200 a year for insurance you'll probably never use. On paper it's a loss. It still feels worth it.

buildup.text: Insurance eliminates a small probability of a huge loss. The possibility effect inflates the fear of that loss.

discovery.text: We're paying to remove dread, not to optimize expected value. Peace of mind has its own price tag.

twist.text: Extended warranties exploit this. The chance of breakdown is tiny, but the pain of losing a new phone feels huge.

climax.text: Ask: can I absorb this loss? If yes, you're paying for emotion, not protection. Sometimes that's fine. Know it.

quiz.question: Why do people overpay for insurance against rare events?
options: Insurance companies set prices too low
We overweight small probabilities of big losses
Rare events are actually very common
